sanskrit: imāṃ kākopamāṃ karṇa procyamānāṃ nibodha me śrutvā yatheṣṭaṃ kuryās tvaṃ vihīna kulapāṃsana
english: Listen to this comparison with a crow that I now set forth, Karṇa; having heard it, do as you please, O base man, defiler of your line.

sanskrit: nāham ātmani kiṃ cid vai kilbiṣaṃ karṇa saṃsmare yena tvaṃ māṃ mahābāho hantum icchasy anāgasam
english: I can recall no fault in myself at all, Karṇa, for which you, O mighty-armed one, should wish to destroy me, who am innocent.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā vācyaṃ budhyatāṃ yadi te hitam viśeṣato rathasthena rājñaś caiva hitaiṣiṇā
english: Yet I must surely speak, if you would understand your own good—and all the more, since I stand upon your chariot and wish the king well.

sanskrit: samaṃ ca viṣamaṃ caiva rathinaś ca balābalam śramaḥ khedaś ca satataṃ hayānāṃ rathinā saha
english: Smooth ground and rough, the strength and weakness of the warrior, the unceasing toil and weariness of the horses together with the chariot-fighter—

sanskrit: āyudhasya parijñānaṃ rutaṃ ca mṛgapakṣiṇām bhāraś cāpy atibhāraś ca śalyānāṃ ca pratikriyā
english: the knowledge of weapons, the cries of beasts and birds, the load and the overload, and the drawing-out of barbs—

sanskrit: astrayogaś ca yuddhaṃ ca nimittāni tathaiva ca sarvam etan mayā jñeyaṃ rathasyāsya kuṭumbinā atas tvāṃ kathaye karṇa nidarśanam idaṃ punaḥ
english: the deployment of missiles, the fighting itself, and the omens too—all this must be known to me, who am as the householder of this chariot. Therefore, Karṇa, I tell you once more this instructive tale.

sanskrit: vaiśyaḥ kila samudrānte prabhūtadhanadhānyavān yajvā dānapatiḥ kṣāntaḥ svakarmastho 'bhavac chuciḥ
english: On the shore of the sea, they say, there dwelt a Vaiśya rich in wealth and grain, a performer of sacrifices, a lord of generosity, patient, steadfast in his own duty, and pure.

sanskrit: bahuputraḥ priyāpatyaḥ sarvabhūtānukampakaḥ rājño dharmapradhānasya rāṣṭre vasati nirbhayaḥ
english: With many sons, fond of his children, compassionate to all beings, he lived without fear in the realm of a king whose chief care was righteousness.

sanskrit: putrāṇāṃ tasya bālānāṃ kumārāṇāṃ yaśasvinām kāko bahūnām abhavad ucciṣṭakṛtabhojanaḥ
english: Of his many young sons, those glorious boys, a crow became the pet, fed on the leavings of their meals.

sanskrit: tasmai sadā prayacchanti vaiśyaputrāḥ kumārakāḥ māṃsodanaṃ dadhi kṣīraṃ pāyasaṃ madhusarpiṣī
english: To it the Vaiśya's young sons would always give meat and rice, curds and milk, sweet milk-pudding, honey and clarified butter.

sanskrit: sa cocchiṣṭabhṛtaḥ kāko vaiśyaputraiḥ kumārakaiḥ sadṛśān pakṣiṇo dṛptaḥ śreyasaś cāvamanyate
english: And that crow, nourished on scraps by the Vaiśya's young sons, grew arrogant and held in contempt the birds that were his equals—and his betters too.

sanskrit: atha haṃsāḥ samudrānte kadā cid abhipātinaḥ garuḍasya gatau tulyāś cakrāṅgā hṛṣṭacetasaḥ
english: Now one day there came flying down to the seashore some swans, swift as Garuḍa in flight, ruddy-limbed and glad of heart.

sanskrit: kumārakās tato haṃsān dṛṣṭvā kākam athābruvan bhavān eva viśiṣṭo hi patatribhyo vihaṃgama
english: Then the boys, seeing the swans, said to the crow: "Surely you, O bird, are the best of all winged creatures!"

sanskrit: pratāryamāṇas tu sa tair alpabuddhibhir aṇḍajaḥ tad vacaḥ satyam ity eva maurkhyād darpāc ca manyate
english: And the egg-born one, beguiled by those witless children, took their words for truth, out of folly and out of pride.

sanskrit: tān so 'bhipatya jijñāsuḥ ka eṣāṃ śreṣṭhabhāg iti ucchiṣṭadarpitaḥ kāko bahūnāṃ dūrapātinām
english: Puffed up by his diet of scraps, the crow flew at those many far-flying birds, eager to learn which among them was the foremost.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yaṃ pravaraṃ mene haṃsānāṃ dūrapātinām tam āhvayata durbuddhiḥ patāma iti pakṣiṇam
english: Whichever of those far-flying swans he judged the best, that bird the dull-witted crow challenged, saying, "Let us fly!"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā prāhasan haṃsā ye tatrāsan samāgatāḥ bhāṣato bahu kākasya balinaḥ patatāṃ varāḥ idam ūcuś ca cakrāṅgā vacaḥ kākaṃ vihaṃgamāḥ
english: Hearing this, the swans gathered there laughed aloud as the crow babbled on; and those mighty, best of fliers, the ruddy-limbed birds, spoke these words to the crow.

sanskrit: vayaṃ haṃsāś carāmemāṃ pṛthivīṃ mānasaukasaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ ca vayaṃ nityaṃ dūrapātena pūjitāḥ
english: "We are swans, dwellers on Lake Mānasa, who roam this whole earth, and we are ever honored among birds for our far-ranging flight.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu haṃsaṃ balinaṃ vajrāṅgaṃ dūrapātinam kāko bhūtvā nipatane samāhvayasi durmate kathaṃ tvaṃ patanaṃ kāka sahāsmābhir bravīṣi tat
english: How is it, fool, that being but a crow, you challenge to a flight the strong, adamant-limbed, far-flying swan? How, crow, do you speak of flying together with us?"

sanskrit: atha haṃsavaco mūḍhaḥ kutsayitvā punaḥ punaḥ prajagādottaraṃ kākaḥ katthano jātilāghavāt
english: Then the foolish, boastful crow, scorning the swan's words again and again, gave his answer out of native frivolity:

sanskrit: śatam ekaṃ ca pātānāṃ patitāsmi na saṃśayaḥ śatayojanam ekaikaṃ vicitraṃ vividhaṃ tathā
english: "A hundred and one styles of flight will I fly, no doubt of it—each one stretching a hundred leagues, varied and of many kinds:

sanskrit: uḍḍīnam avaḍīnaṃ ca praḍīnaṃ ḍīnam eva ca niḍīnam atha saṃḍīnaṃ tiryak cātigatāni ca
english: the up-flight and the down-flight, the forth-flight and the plain flight, the low-flight and the close-flight, the sidelong and the soaring courses;

sanskrit: viḍīnaṃ pariḍīnaṃ ca parāḍīnaṃ suḍīnakam atiḍīnaṃ mahāḍīnaṃ niḍīnaṃ pariḍīnakam
english: the spread-flight and the round-flight, the away-flight and the deft-flight, the high-flight and the great-flight, the swoop and the wheeling;

sanskrit: gatāgatapratigatā bahvīś ca nikuḍīnikāḥ kartāsmi miṣatāṃ vo 'dya tato drakṣyatha me balam
english: the goings and comings and returnings, and many a downward dart—all these I shall perform before your very eyes this day, and then you shall behold my power."

sanskrit: evam ukte tu kākena prahasyaiko vihaṃgamaḥ uvāca haṃsas taṃ kākaṃ vacanaṃ tan nibodha me
english: When the crow had spoken thus, one of the birds, a swan, laughed and answered the crow—hear that speech from me:

sanskrit: śatam ekaṃ ca pātānāṃ tvaṃ kāka patitā dhruvam ekam eva tu ye pātaṃ viduḥ sarve vihaṃgamāḥ
english: "A hundred and one styles of flight you, crow, will surely fly; but all birds know only one single style of flight,

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ patitā kāka nānyaṃ jānāmi kaṃ cana pata tvam api raktākṣa yena vā tena manyase
english: and that one alone shall I fly, crow; no other do I know. As for you, red-eyed one, fly by whatever style you fancy."

sanskrit: atha kākāḥ prajahasur ye tatrāsan samāgatāḥ katham ekena pātena haṃsaḥ pātaśataṃ jayet
english: Then the crows gathered there burst out laughing: "How shall a swan with a single style of flight outdo a hundred styles?

sanskrit: ekenaiva śatasyaikaṃ pātenābhibhaviṣyati haṃsasya patitaṃ kāko balavān āśuvikramaḥ
english: With one flight against a hundred, the strong, swift-striding crow will overmatch the swan's single flight!"

sanskrit: prapetatuḥ spardhayātha tatas tau haṃsavāyasau ekapātī ca cakrāṅgaḥ kākaḥ pātaśatena ca
english: So then the swan and the crow flew off in contest—the ruddy-limbed swan with his one flight, and the crow with his hundred.

sanskrit: petivān atha cakrāṅgaḥ petivān atha vāyasaḥ visismāpayiṣuḥ pātair ācakṣāṇo ''tmanaḥ kriyām
english: The ruddy-limbed one flew, and the crow flew too, eager to amaze with his flights, proclaiming his own performance.

sanskrit: atha kākasya citrāṇi patitānītarāṇi ca dṛṣṭvā pramuditāḥ kākā vinedur atha taiḥ svaraiḥ
english: Then, seeing the crow's flights, dazzling and diverse, the crows rejoiced and cried out with their cawings,

sanskrit: haṃsāṃś cāvahasanti sma prāvadann apriyāṇi ca utpatyotpatya ca prāhur muhūrtam iti ceti ca
english: jeering at the swans and uttering insults; flying up again and again, they called out, "In a moment! And like this! And like that!"

sanskrit: vṛkṣāgrebhyaḥ sthalebhyaś ca nipatanty utpatanti ca kurvāṇā vividhān rāvān āśaṃsantas tadā jayam
english: From treetops and from level ground they swooped down and soared up, raising their varied clamor, confident then of victory.

sanskrit: haṃsas tu mṛdukenaiva vikrāntum upacakrame pratyahīyata kākāc ca muhūrtam iva māriṣa
english: But the swan set out to fly with a gentle, easy stroke, and for a moment, sir, he fell behind the crow.

sanskrit: avamanya rayaṃ haṃsān idaṃ vacanam abravīt yo 'sāv utpatito haṃsaḥ so 'sāv eva prahīyate
english: Despising the swans' pace, the crow spoke these words: "That swan who flew up yonder—why, the very same now lags behind!"

sanskrit: atha haṃsaḥ sa tac chrutvā prāpatat paścimāṃ diśam upary upari vegena sāgaraṃ varuṇālayam
english: Then the swan, hearing this, set off toward the western quarter, speeding higher and higher over the ocean, the abode of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: tato bhīḥ prāviśat kākaṃ tadā tatra vicetasam dvīpadrumān apaśyantaṃ nipatantaṃ śramānvitam nipateyaṃ kva nu śrānta iti tasmiñ jalārṇave
english: Then fear entered the crow, bewildered out there, seeing no island, no tree, sinking down worn out: "Where, weary as I am, can I come to rest upon this watery deep?"

sanskrit: aviṣahyaḥ samudro hi bahusattvagaṇālayaḥ mahābhūtaśatodbhāsī nabhaso 'pi viśiṣyate
english: For the sea is not to be withstood, the home of many a host of creatures, gleaming with hundreds of great beings—it surpasses even the sky.

sanskrit: gāmbhīryād dhi samudrasya na viśeṣaḥ kulādhama digambarāmbhasāṃ karṇa samudrasthā hi durjayāḥ vidūrapātāt toyasya kiṃ punaḥ karṇa vāyasaḥ
english: By reason of the sea's depth, O lowest of your line, there is no telling its waters from the wide horizon's robe; for they who dwell upon the sea, Karṇa, are hard to conquer—how much more so a crow far out over the deep, Karṇa?

sanskrit: atha haṃso 'bhyatikramya muhūrtam iti ceti ca avekṣamāṇas taṃ kākaṃ nāśaknod vyapasarpitum atikramya ca cakrāṅgaḥ kākaṃ taṃ samudaikṣata
english: Then the swan, having outstripped him in a moment, looked back upon the crow, who—try as he might—could not get away; and the ruddy-limbed one, having passed him, gazed upon that crow.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā hīyamānaṃ ca haṃso dṛṣṭvābravīd idam ujjihīrṣur nimajjantaṃ smaran satpuruṣavratam
english: And seeing him thus falling behind, the swan, mindful of the vow of the virtuous and wishing to lift up the sinking bird, spoke these words:

sanskrit: bahūni patanāni tvam ācakṣāṇo muhur muhuḥ patasy avyāharaṃś cedaṃ na no guhyaṃ prabhāṣase
english: "Boasting of your many flights again and again, you now fly without naming them; this secret art you do not declare to us at all.

sanskrit: kiṃ nāma patanaṃ kāka yat tvaṃ patasi sāṃpratam jalaṃ spṛśasi pakṣābhyāṃ tuṇḍena ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: What style of flight, O crow, is this that you now fly, touching the water with both wings and with your beak again and again?"

sanskrit: sa pakṣābhyāṃ spṛśann ārtas tuṇḍena jalam arṇave kāko dṛḍhaṃ pariśrāntaḥ sahasā nipapāta ha
english: Touching the water of the sea with his wings and his beak, that crow, in distress and utterly spent, suddenly dropped down.

sanskrit: haṃsa uvāca śatam ekaṃ ca pātānāṃ yat prabhāṣasi vāyasa nānāvidhānīha purā tac cānṛtam ihādya te
english: The swan said: "Those hundred and one styles of flight, crow, of which you boasted just now, in all their variety—here, today, they are proved a lie in you."

sanskrit: kāka uvāca ucchiṣṭadarpito haṃsa manye ''tmānaṃ suparṇavat avamanya bahūṃś cāhaṃ kākān anyāṃś ca pakṣiṇaḥ prāṇair haṃsa prapadye tvāṃ dvīpāntaṃ prāpayasva mām
english: The crow said: "Made proud by my diet of scraps, O swan, I deemed myself the equal of Garuḍa, and looked down on many crows and on other birds besides. For my very life, swan, I throw myself upon you—carry me to the shore of an island!"

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ svastimān haṃsa svadeśaṃ prāpnuyāṃ punaḥ na kaṃ cid avamanyeyam āpado māṃ samuddhara
english: "If, swan, I should come safe again to my own country, never again would I despise anyone. Lift me out of this calamity!"

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ dīnaṃ vilapantam acetanam kāka kāketi vāśantaṃ nimajjantaṃ mahārṇave
english: As he spoke thus, wretched, wailing, witless, croaking "Caw, caw!" and sinking in the great deep,

sanskrit: tathaitya vāyasaṃ haṃso jalaklinnaṃ sudurdaśam padbhyām utkṣipya vepantaṃ pṛṣṭham āropayac chanaiḥ
english: the swan came up to the crow—drenched and pitiable to behold—and lifting the trembling creature with his feet, he set him gently upon his back.

sanskrit: āropya pṛṣṭhaṃ kākaṃ taṃ haṃsaḥ karṇa vicetasam ājagāma punar dvīpaṃ spardhayā petatur yataḥ
english: Having set the dazed crow upon his back, the swan, Karṇa, came back to the island from which the two had set out in their contest.

sanskrit: saṃsthāpya taṃ cāpi punaḥ samāśvāsya ca khecaram gato yathepsitaṃ deśaṃ haṃso mana ivāśugaḥ
english: And having set that bird down again and comforted him, the swan, swift as thought, departed to the region he desired.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭabhojanāt kāko yathā vaiśyakule tu saḥ evaṃ tvam ucchiṣṭabhṛto dhārtarāṣṭrair na saṃśayaḥ sadṛśāñ śreyasaś cāpi sarvān karṇātimanyase
english: As that crow in the Vaiśya's house grew proud from feeding on scraps, even so are you, Karṇa, nourished on scraps by Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons—no doubt of it—and you despise all your equals and your betters alike.

sanskrit: droṇadrauṇikṛpair gupto bhīṣmeṇānyaiś ca kauravaiḥ virāṭanagare pārtham ekaṃ kiṃ nāvadhīs tadā
english: Guarded by Droṇa, Aśvatthāman, and Kṛpa, by Bhīṣma and the other Kauravas—why then did you not slay the lone Pārtha in Virāṭa's city?

sanskrit: yatra vyastāḥ samastāś ca nirjitāḥ stha kirīṭinā sṛgālā iva siṃhena kva te vīryam abhūt tadā
english: There, scattered and gathered alike, you were all vanquished by the Diademed One, like jackals by a lion. Where then was that valor of yours?

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ ca hataṃ dṛṣṭvā nirjitaḥ savyasācinā paśyatāṃ kuruvīrāṇāṃ prathamaṃ tvaṃ palāyathāḥ
english: And seeing your brother slain, defeated by the Left-handed Archer, before the very eyes of the Kuru heroes you were the first to flee.

sanskrit: tathā dvaitavane karṇa gandharvaiḥ samabhidrutaḥ kurūn samagrān utsṛjya prathamaṃ tvaṃ palāyathāḥ
english: So too in the Dvaita forest, Karṇa, when the Gandharvas fell upon you, abandoning all the Kurus you were the first to flee.

sanskrit: hatvā jitvā ca gandharvāṃś citrasenamukhān raṇe karṇa duryodhanaṃ pārthaḥ sabhāryaṃ samamocayat
english: Smiting and conquering the Gandharvas led by Citrasena in battle, Karṇa, it was Pārtha who set Duryodhana free, together with his wives.

sanskrit: punaḥ prabhāvaḥ pārthasya purāṇaḥ keśavasya ca kathitaḥ karṇa rāmeṇa sabhāyāṃ rājasaṃsadi
english: And once again, Karṇa, the ancient might of Pārtha and of Keśava was recounted by Rāma in the hall, in the assembly of kings.

sanskrit: satataṃ ca tad aśrauṣīr vacanaṃ droṇabhīṣmayoḥ avadhyau vadatoḥ kṛṣṇau saṃnidhau vai mahīkṣitām
english: And ever did you hear that word of Droṇa and Bhīṣma, declaring before the kings that the two Kṛṣṇas could not be slain.

sanskrit: kiyantaṃ tatra vakṣyāmi yena yena dhanaṃjayaḥ tvatto 'tiriktaḥ sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo brāhmaṇo yathā
english: How much shall I tell of all the ways in which Dhanaṃjaya surpasses you, surpasses all beings, as the brahmin surpasses every other?

sanskrit: idānīm eva draṣṭāsi pradhane syandane sthitau putraṃ ca vasudevasya pāṇḍavaṃ ca dhanaṃjayam
english: This very moment you shall behold them, stationed on their chariot in the forefront of battle—the son of Vāsudeva and the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: devāsuramanuṣyeṣu prakhyātau yau nararṣabhau prakāśenābhivikhyātau tvaṃ tu khadyotavan nṛṣu
english: Those two bulls among men, renowned among gods, demons, and mortals, blaze forth in their splendor; but you are like a firefly among men.

sanskrit: evaṃ vidvān māvamaṃsthāḥ sūtaputrācyutārjunau nṛsiṃhau tau naraśvā tvaṃ joṣam āssva vikatthana
english: Knowing this, O son of a charioteer, do not slight Acyuta and Arjuna. They are lions among men, and you a mere cur; so hold your peace, boaster.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca madrādhipasyādhirathis tadaivaṃ; vaco niśamyāpriyam apratītaḥ uvāca śalyaṃ viditaṃ mamaitad; yathāvidhāv arjunavāsudevau
english: Saṃjaya said: When the son of Adhiratha had thus heard the unwelcome speech of the lord of the Madras, unabashed he answered Śalya: "This is well known to me—what manner of men are Arjuna and Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: śaure rathaṃ vāhayato 'rjunasya; balaṃ mahāstrāṇi ca pāṇḍavasya ahaṃ vijānāmi yathāvad adya; parokṣabhūtaṃ tava tat tu śalya
english: The strength of the Pāṇḍava Arjuna, and his great weapons, while Śauri drives his chariot—all this I rightly know this day, Śalya, though to you it lies beyond your sight.

sanskrit: tau cāpradhṛṣyau śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhau; vyapetabhīr yodhayiṣyāmi kṛṣṇau saṃtāpayaty abhyadhikaṃ tu rāmāc; chāpo 'dya māṃ brāhmaṇasattamāc ca
english: Unassailable though they are, the best of all who bear arms, those two Kṛṣṇas I shall fight without fear; yet what torments me far more this day is the curse from Rāma and from that best of brahmins.

sanskrit: avātsaṃ vai brāhmaṇacchadmanāhaṃ; rāme purā divyam astraṃ cikīrṣuḥ tatrāpi me devarājena vighno; hitārthinā phalgunasyaiva śalya
english: Long ago I dwelt with Rāma in the guise of a brahmin, wishing to master the celestial weapon; and there too, Śalya, the king of the gods cast a hindrance in my path, seeking only Phalguna's good.

sanskrit: kṛto 'vabhedena mamorum etya; praviśya kīṭasya tanuṃ virūpām guror bhayāc cāpi na celivān ahaṃ; tac cāvabuddho dadṛśe sa vipraḥ
english: Entering my thigh in the misshapen body of a worm, he bored it through; yet out of fear of my teacher I did not stir, and the brahmin, awakening, beheld it.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaś cāhaṃ tam avocaṃ maharṣiṃ; sūto 'ham asmīti sa māṃ śaśāpa sūtopadhāv āptam idaṃ tvayāstraṃ; na karmakāle pratibhāsyati tvām
english: Questioned, I told that great sage, "I am a charioteer's son." Then he cursed me: "This weapon, won by you through a charioteer's deceit, shall not come to your mind at the hour of need."

sanskrit: anyatra yasmāt tava mṛtyukālād; abrāhmaṇe brahma na hi dhruvaṃ syāt tad adya paryāptam atīva śastram; asmin saṃgrāme tumule tāta bhīme
english: "Save only at the hour of your death—for the sacred power cannot abide unfailing in one who is no brahmin." Yet even so, this weapon will more than suffice this day, in this tumultuous and terrible battle, my friend.

sanskrit: apāṃ patir vegavān aprameyo; nimajjayiṣyan nivahān prajānām mahānagaṃ yaḥ kurute samudraṃ; velaiva taṃ vārayaty aprameyam
english: As the swift and measureless lord of waters, the sea—who would drown whole hosts of creatures and swells into a vast mountain—is yet held back by the shore alone, immeasurable though he be,

sanskrit: pramuñcantaṃ bāṇasaṃghān amoghān; marmacchido vīrahaṇaḥ sapatrān kuntīputraṃ pratiyotsyāmi yuddhe; jyākarṣiṇām uttamam adya loke
english: so shall I give battle to the son of Kuntī, slayer of heroes, as he looses his unerring, feathered shafts that cleave the vital points—he who is the foremost bow-drawer in the world this day.

sanskrit: evaṃ balenātibalaṃ mahāstraṃ; samudrakalpaṃ sudurāpam ugram śaraughiṇaṃ pārthivān majjayantaṃ; veleva pārtham iṣubhiḥ saṃsahiṣye
english: With my own strength I shall withstand that mighty one, surpassing in might, wielder of the great weapon, like unto the sea, terrible and most hard to face, who in floods of arrows drowns the kings—Pārtha I shall meet with my shafts, as the shore meets the ocean.

sanskrit: adyāhave yasya na tulyam anyaṃ; manye manuṣyaṃ dhanur ādadānam surāsurān vai yudhi yo jayeta; tenādya me paśya yuddhaṃ sughoram
english: In battle this day, against him whose equal among men, when he takes up the bow, I deem there is none—who in war could vanquish gods and demons alike—against him behold this day my most dreadful combat.

sanskrit: atimānī pāṇḍavo yuddhakāmo; amānuṣair eṣyati me mahāstraiḥ tasyāstram astrair abhihatya saṃkhye; śarottamaiḥ pātayiṣyāmi pārtham
english: The over-proud Pāṇḍava, eager for the fight, will come against me with his superhuman great weapons; striking down his missiles with my own in the fray, with my choicest shafts I shall lay Pārtha low.

sanskrit: divākareṇāpi samaṃ tapantaṃ; samāptaraśmiṃ yaśasā jvalantam tamonudaṃ megha ivātimātro; dhanaṃjayaṃ chādayiṣyāmi bāṇaiḥ
english: Him who blazes hot as the very sun, his rays at their full, flaming with glory, dispeller of darkness—Dhanaṃjaya I shall veil with my arrows, as a boundless cloud veils the sun.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaraṃ dhūmaśikhaṃ jvalantaṃ; tejasvinaṃ lokam imaṃ dahantam megho bhūtvā śaravarṣair yathāgniṃ; tathā pārthaṃ śamayiṣyāmi yuddhe
english: As one might become a cloud and with showers of rain quench the fire—Vaiśvānara, his crest of smoke ablaze, radiant, consuming this whole world—so with showers of arrows shall I quell Pārtha in battle.

sanskrit: pramāthinaṃ balavantaṃ prahāriṇaṃ; prabhañjanaṃ mātariśvānam ugram yuddhe sahiṣye himavān ivācalo; dhanaṃjayaṃ kruddham amṛṣyamāṇam
english: The crushing, mighty, smiting one—the rending wind, fierce Mātariśvan—even him in battle I shall withstand, as the unmoving Himālaya withstands the gale: Dhanaṃjaya enraged and unforgiving.

sanskrit: viśāradaṃ rathamārgeṣv asaktaṃ; dhuryaṃ nityaṃ samareṣu pravīram loke varaṃ sarvadhanurdharāṇāṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ saṃyuge saṃsahiṣye
english: Skilled and unhampered in the ways of chariot-warfare, ever the foremost champion in battles, the best in the world of all who bear the bow—Dhanaṃjaya I shall withstand in the fray.
